answer.held_back_by: I think being straight and honest cost me STAND, so the system seems to reward playing safe more than being correct. I topped out as Minister but never felt like I was getting ahead, and I never really understood what the grades meant.
answer.ending_fair_why: I made it to Minister with 100 integrity and that matches how I played. The ending card was dry and a bit funny, though I still don't know why STAND kept sliding, so the game didn't fully explain itself.
answer.chase_next: I'd try the ending where I play politics and pad things, to see if STAND goes up and whether it costs me integrity. I want to know if honesty really was the problem.
answer.play_again_why: It was fun in bursts, but the late years felt repetitive and I'd want a break first. Maybe later, once I forget how the grades work.
answer.title_fit_why: The pay packages and lifetime earnings were what I tracked and talked about with my friend. 'Confirmed & Substantive' sounds like civil service jargon that I only half understand.
